messages:
emma: heads up — email preview embed requests are coming into attachment-proxy with external Referer headers that include a URL fragment that looks like a session token. proxy appears to be resolving the URL and calling internal storage. unsure if token is real or just client-side artifact.

raj: can you paste the raw headers and the proxy log line?

emma: sure, here's the header we see in logs:

```http
GET /v1/fetch?url=https://s3.external/bucket/obj.jpg HTTP/1.1
Host: proxy.internal
Referer: https://mail.external/messages/123#session=eyJhbGciOiJI...
User-Agent: Redwood-MailClient/2.3
X-Forwarded-For: 10.4.3.2
```

emma: proxy log line: `fetch_service: fetcher=attachment-proxy url=https://s3.external/bucket/obj.jpg upstream_status=200 downstream_request=http://internal-storage.local/objects/abcd` — it expands the URL and requested an internal host.

oliver: this looks like SSRF + authz exposure if fragments are being interpreted server-side. browsers don't send fragments, so client must be encoding it into the URL or proxy is reconstructing it.

jen: oncall, is this actively exploitable? any signs of access to internal-only endpoints?

emma: saw one request to `http://internal-storage.local/healthz` (200) around 1843104200 which shouldn't be reachable.

raj: immediate containment: disable public email preview rendering for 10m and block the proxy's outbound egress to internal-storage host via firewall. @oliver can you push a quick ACL?

oliver: on it. adding temporary egress deny for proxy -> internal-storage (rule tmp-block-184310). ETA ~3m.

security-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-EMB-001. Severity: high. SOC notified.

sara: heads-up to support — pausing email preview feature for all orgs to avoid potential PII leakage. drafting cust comms.

raj: also search logs for `Referer` and `#session=` patterns in last 30 days and grep proxy requests for internal hostnames. assigning to me + emma.

emma: starting search, saving hits to drive: https://redwood.local/drive/incident/SEC-2026-EMB-001

oliver: egress rule applied and verified — no further calls to internal-storage from proxy since 1843104500. rolling a proxy patch to strip fragments and reject URLs containing `#`.

jen: good. next steps: 1) full audit of token formats seen, 2) KMS rotation of any exposed keys, 3) temporary revocation of suspect session tokens, 4) postmortem + CVE triage if required.

raj: also check RBAC/audit logs for anomalous access around those timestamps; if we see internal authed calls treat as credential leak.

emma: initial log search found ~4 requests with `#session=` coming from same client IP range. tokens look JWT-like. handing samples to forensics.

sara: support comms ready. propose message: "we paused preview rendering after detecting requests that may contain session identifiers; investigating and will update in 2 hours."

oliver: PR to sanitize proxy input: strip URL fragments, refuse URLs with `#` in them, validate host against allowed list. deploying to canary now.

security-bot: Update: canary passed, deploying to 80% at 1843105600.

raj: creating followups: SEC-2026-EMB-002 (forensic), SEC-2026-EMB-003 (KMS/key rotation), SEC-2026-EMB-004 (postmortem). @emma please assign owners.

emma: assigned. I'll lead the postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jen: after containment let's run an audit of other server-side fetchers (image proxy, OG preview, link unfurl) to ensure they don't accept fragments or resolve to internal hostnames.
